concept.name: HODL waves
concept.definition: HODL waves are a visualization of the age distribution of the coin supply: colored bands show what fraction of all coins last moved within each age bucket (from <1 day to >10 years), revealing accumulation and distribution cycles.
concept.intuition: It is a geological cross-section of holder behavior: warm young layers swell when coins churn, cool old layers thicken when conviction holders sit tight.
concept.mechanics: Each band's thickness is the share of total supply whose last on-chain movement falls in that age band (bands: <1d, 1d-1w, 1w-1m, 1-3m, 3-6m, 6-12m, 1-2y, 2-3y, 3-5y, 5-7y, 7-10y, >10y). Young bands swell near bull-market tops as old coins are spent and reactivated; old bands thicken in bear markets as accumulation matures into dormancy.
concept.failure_modes: Movement-based aging resets a coin's age even for self-transfers and exchange reshuffles, so apparent 'reactivation' may be pure custody plumbing; bands lag reality by construction — coins must survive to a band's lower bound before appearing in it.
concept.misconceptions: Thickening old bands do not prove accumulation by smart money — they also include lost coins, which grow monotonically and are often assumed out of circulation. HODL waves describe structure, not timing.
concept.example: At bull-market peaks, the <6-month bands have historically swollen toward 50%+ of supply as long-term holders distributed; in deep bear markets, 1y+ bands thicken as coins migrate into cold storage and mature.

citations.source: Glassnode Docs - HODL Waves metric guide
